figures.bridge_line: the farmer who gave everything away and went out - the figure through whom this city's church told itself what the desert meant

dates.born: c. 251 (convention, derived from the Vita's 105-year claim)
dates.floruit: the emblem of the emerging desert movement, c. 270-356; known to this world chiefly through Athanasius's portrait (c. 356-362)

figures.bridge_line: the bishop who spent forty-six embattled years holding the line drawn at Nicaea - and who wrote the treatise this world's Center answers from

dates.died: 373 (consensus), 'in the second consulate of Gratian and Probus... having governed that church amidst the greatest perils forty-six years' (Socrates HE IV.20, npnf202 lines 13310-13322, verified; NOTE: that edition's own editor note reads the consulate as 371 and flags Jerome's Chronicle as discordant - the discrepancy is stated, not resolved)
dates.floruit: bishop 328-373, exiled five times; the dominant late-horizon voice

figures.bridge_line: the teacher whose books survive where his life does not - his words are kept, his days are not

dates.died: c. 215 (convention; the NPNF De viris 38 editor annotates 'born about 160, died about 217' - an editorial note, not Jerome's text)
dates.floruit: c. 180-202/3 teaching in Alexandria (left during the Severan persecution); Jerome De viris 38: pupil of Pantaenus, led the school after his master's death

names.name: Clement of Alexandria (Titus Flavius Clemens, c. 150-c. 215)

figures.bridge_line: the bishop of forty-three years whose office collided with the school's greatest teacher

dates.died: 232 (derived: accession under Commodus's tenth year, HE V.22 - this edition's editor computes 189 - plus 'held the office for forty-three full years', HE VI.26, npnf201 line 36336, verified)
dates.floruit: bishop of Alexandria 189-232; the bishop of the Origen rupture

figures.bridge_line: the blind teacher who held the school's chair for fifty years, engaging Scripture through hearing and memory - the tradition's last great voice in this window, whose own books time nearly erased

dates.born: c. 309-313 (derived from two primary attestations: Jerome De viris 109, written 392/3, 'has already passed his eighty-third year'; Palladius, Lausiac History IV, 85 at death)
dates.died: c. 398 (Palladius: 'He was 85 years old when he died')
dates.floruit: head of the Alexandrian teaching tradition for roughly half a century, to 398; blind from age four ('so he told me' - Palladius, eyewitness)

figures.bridge_line: the teacher-become-bishop who led the church through plague and persecution, and answered a book against allegory with three days of patient listening

dates.floruit: head of the teaching tradition, then bishop c. 248-264: the Decian persecution, the lapsed controversy, the plague, the Nepos affair

names.name: Dionysius of Alexandria ('the Great', bishop c. 248-264)

figures.bridge_line: the student who told us, in his own voice, what it was to be taught - the one first-person account of this school's formation

dates.floruit: student under Origen at Caesarea c. 233-238; the Address of Thanksgiving delivered c. 238 (Nautin's authenticity/dating dispute noted; consensus reaffirms)

figures.bridge_line: the pupil who took first the teacher's chair and then the bishop's - the school and the office joined in one man

dates.floruit: Origen's assistant then successor in the school; succeeded Demetrius as bishop 232 (HE VI.26)

figures.bridge_line: the school's greatest and most contested teacher - a man the tradition revered, inherited, cautioned about, and in part later condemned, all within living memory of his chair

dates.born: c. 185 (derived: HE VII.1 has him dying at 69 under Gallus, 251-253)
dates.died: c. 253/4, Tyre, after imprisonment and torture under Decius - 'At this time Origen died, being sixty-nine years of age' (HE VII.1, npnf201 line 39163, verified verbatim)
dates.floruit: head of catechetical instruction from his eighteenth year (HE VI.3, npnf201 line 32732, verified); Alexandria until the Demetrius rupture c. 231-234, then Caesarea

figures.bridge_line: the first teacher of this school whose name was kept - a converted Stoic philosopher, remembered by his pupil as the bee who gathered honey from the prophets and apostles

dates.died: before c. 215 (inference from succession notices only)
dates.floruit: c. 180-200: Eusebius HE V.10 places him heading the school under Commodus; Jerome De viris 36 has him teaching 'in the reigns of the emperor Severus and Antoninus surnamed Caracalla' (193-217)
